subject: Urgent: CrescentRX live incidents — streaming timeouts & retry amplification (exec call requested)
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@crescentrx.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: David Kline <david.kline@crescentrx.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production: repeated streaming timeouts affecting Rx approvals

Jordan —

We're seeing a sharp increase in failed streaming completions from your hosted API this afternoon. Our clinical UI gets a 5xx/429 cascade and many sessions are dropping after ~10–15s. The result: nurses can't complete approvals and our throughput drops ~30% during peaks. This started ~14:45 PST and has been intermittent since then. We opened a ticket (SUP-11924) but this is causing immediate clinical workflow impact.

Can you confirm this is on your side and whether there's an immediate mitigation we can apply? We need a short call with your team + our CTO in the next hour.

—Elena
Director, Digital Ops — CrescentRX

Attachments: crescentrx-screenshots-14-45.png (screenshot, referenced)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@crescentrx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 16:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: repeated streaming timeouts affecting Rx approvals

Elena — thanks for the heads up and I'm sorry for the disruption. Monica and Rishi are on call and triaging now.

Immediate next steps (we'll confirm in the call):
- Stand up a 30-min bridge now (zoom link below) for real-time triage with your team and our engineers.
- Short-term mitigations to try while we investigate: increase client SDK stream keepalive to 60s, disable aggressive client-side retry (backoff to 3s with jitter), and we can flip a regional routing policy to route your traffic to a warmed dedicated pool.
- We will prepare an incident summary and a proposed MAP with milestones and remediation tasks.

Can you confirm the Zoom availability? If so we'll join ASAP.

Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/987654321
SUP ticket: SUP-11924

Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0179

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 16:35:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Production: repeated streaming timeouts affecting Rx approvals

On Sat, Feb 27, 2027 at 4:22 PM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Immediate next steps (we'll confirm in the call):

Quick triage notes from infra:
- Observed a 12:21–16:30 PST spike in 500/429 originating from the gateway layer terminating long-lived streaming sockets. Error rate peaked at ~8% for your tenant and coincides with a client SDK retry pattern amplifying requests.
- Primary signal: upstream keepalive timeouts on the L4 proxy + abrupt client reconnects causing KV cache churn inside the serving runtime. This produces shorter-lived sessions and increased token re-computation which drives CPU and memory pressure.
- Secondary: our autoscaler briefly undershot desired warmed capacity for the region during the surge (we have metrics + graph in the attachment).

Short-term mitigations we've just executed:
1) Increased proxy keepalive from 20s -> 65s for traffic tagged to CrescentRX (should reduce idle disconnects).
2) Applied a temporary per-tenant concurrency cap and prioritized interactive sessions to keep latency SLOs intact.
3) Disabled an experimental aggressive KV-sync that was recently rolled to the pool your traffic hit.

Consequence: we expect error-rate to fall within 20–30 minutes as warmed pool and keepalive take effect. If not, next steps are rolling a fallback to an older model variant without the recent KV-sync optimizations.

Attaching: crescentrx-incident-summary-20270227.pdf (analysis + graphs).

Monica Patel
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 17:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: repeated streaming timeouts affecting Rx approvals

Folks —

Thanks, Monica — good triage. Two asks for exec/leadership consideration:
1) Approve a 10% one-time account credit for CrescentRX for today's outage while we investigate root cause and confirm SLA impact. I recommend approving fast to avoid escalation to procurement/legal.
2) Assign DRI for postmortem and timelines: engineering (Marissa) + infra (Monica) + account lead (Jordan). I'll coordinate incident postmortem and causal analysis.

Short mitigations to communicate to the customer now (we should send these as a single note):
- Increase SDK keepalive / disable aggressive client retry
- Apply our temporary concurrency cap (already applied)
- Optional route to dedicated warmed pool (requires signup but we can enable emergency routing for 48h)

If the customer agrees to the emergency routing we should schedule the config change during the call (zero downtime).

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@crescentrx.com>, David Kline <david.kline@crescentrx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 17:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: repeated streaming timeouts affecting Rx approvals

Elena —

Thanks for your patience. Monica pushed the keepalive and applied the temporary concurrency cap. We're seeing error-rate decline from 8% -> 1.9% over the last 15 minutes; user reports are starting to normalize.

We propose a 30-minute exec/technical call at 17:40 PST to confirm stability, review the attached incident summary, and decide on a short MAP (we've prepared a draft).

One additional ask: for immediate customer assurance we're prepared to apply emergency routing to a warmed dedicated pool for 24–72 hours. This will incur a temporary charge; Rishi has proposed a 10% one-time credit while we validate. Please let us know if you want us to enable that now — we can do it during the call.

Zoom (same link): https://zoom.us/j/987654321

—Jordan

Thanks for the quick response and for the temporary mitigations. We joined the call and saw the improvements; the clinical teams report significantly fewer failures. CrescentRX accepts the temporary routing to the warmed pool for 48 hours — please proceed. We also accept the proposed one-time credit pending the postmortem.

Next steps agreed on the call (summarized):

- Redwood to produce a postmortem and share by EOD Monday (Mar 1) with root cause, timeline, and remediation steps.
- Follow-up operational items in the MAP spreadsheet attached.

Appreciate the responsiveness. We'll keep SUP-11924 open for any regressions.

—Elena
Director, Digital Ops — CrescentRX
